name: Kenai Fjords National Park
blurb: Glacier meltwater feeds plankton, salmon, sea otters, whales and bears.

tip.title: Dim the glacial meltwater
tip.text: Meltwater from the Harding Icefield carries minerals that support phytoplankton. Set Glacial meltwater to -50% and watch plankton, krill, sand lance and the whales and seabirds that follow.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Long summer days power plankton blooms in the fjords and plant growth on the shores.
Runoff from the Harding Icefield glaciers carries rock flour minerals into the fjords. The park page says this supports phytoplankton.
Bare ground left by retreating glaciers gains soil as lichens, mosses and nitrogen-fixing alders arrive, and later supports forest.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and spawned-out salmon, returning nutrients to the soil and streams.
Drifting algae that bloom in the fjords and nearshore waters, fed in part by minerals in glacial meltwater. They are the base of the marine food web.
A tall wildflower that colonizes open, disturbed ground such as newly exposed land.
The dominant conifer of the coastal forest, which develops on ground that glaciers have left behind.

nodes.name: Krill and zooplankton
nodes.desc: Small drifting crustaceans that graze phytoplankton. They feed humpback whales, young salmon, puffins and schooling fish.
A steep-terrain herbivore that grazes grasses, herbs and shrubs, and browses conifer twigs. Bears and eagles may take kids.
Eats mostly marine invertebrates such as urchins, crabs, clams and mussels. Orcas are its main predator.
A gulp-feeder that eats krill and small schooling fish such as herring and sand lance. Orcas hunt calves.
Eats mostly fish, then waterfowl and other birds, and scavenges carrion. Often steals food from other animals.
The top marine predator of the park waters. GloBI records show it eating whales, seals, sea lions, porpoises and sea otters.
An omnivore that eats salmon, berries, marmots and mountain goats. It carries salmon carcasses into the forest.
